questions.title: What should Shatter do?
questions.context: Shatter needs one honest combat identity before the final combat-tree consumer can be implemented. The current name and Crush branch suggest that it should still be a strike.
questions.recommendation: Keep it as a weak Crush strike. On a landed hit, it also removes 4 armour for the rest of the encounter.

choices.title: Strike and break armour
choices.detail: Raw-power-4 Crush hit; if it lands, remove 4 current armour for this encounter.

choices.title: Armour break only
choices.detail: Deal no damage; remove 4 current armour. Shatter would lose its Strike identity.

choices.title: Keep it unresolved
choices.detail: Leave Shatter unimplemented while the other combat-tree consumers continue.

questions.title: What should Distiller do?
questions.context: Distiller should improve the value of prepared weapon coatings without creating a new affliction or turning the passive into a generic damage bonus.
questions.recommendation: When the owner applies a coating to their own physical weapon, one item should arm two successful-hit charges instead of one.

choices.title: Two successful hits
choices.detail: A self-applied coating lasts for the next two landed weapon hits.

choices.title: Longer affliction
choices.detail: The coating remains one charge, but its resulting affliction lasts longer.

choices.title: Keep it unresolved
choices.detail: Leave Distiller inactive until coating balance has more playtest evidence.

questions.title: How should Reforge progress?
questions.context: The current three +0.2-power ranks do not create three honest upgrades. A weapon gets no final attack increase at rank 1, +1 at rank 2, and still only +1 at rank 3, even though every step costs increasingly scarce materials and Essence.
questions.recommendation: Replace the three-rank meter with one deliberate +0.5-power Reforge at the current first-step price. Preserve every old paid rank at its exact existing power.

choices.title: One meaningful Reforge
choices.detail: One +0.5-power upgrade for 2 qualifying samples and 8 Essence; old paid power migrates exactly.

choices.title: Keep three distinct ranks
choices.detail: Keep three purchases, but redesign each one to have a visible rules-owned effect without duplicating construction tiers.

choices.title: Leave the current meter
choices.detail: Keep +0.2 per rank even though some paid ranks do not change final combat numbers.

choices.title: Keep it unresolved
choices.detail: Do not change Reforge until more equipment balance evidence exists.

questions.title: Which Penmanship prices should we playtest?
questions.context: The inherited 150-Essence Brush would cost about 4.5 fully explored ordinary worlds by itself, or about 6.4 worlds together with its required Scriptorium, before paying to write any new worlds. It also gates Ink Mixing, compounds, Chaining, and the Fountain Pen.
questions.recommendation: Use the complete lower comparison profile as reversible playtest tuning: Brush 45, stable table 70, Ink Mixing 40, Compound Assembly 55, Chaining 90, ruling frame 140, and Fountain Pen 220 Essence. Keep the Scriptorium at 60. Judge the route with real continuation telemetry before final tuning.

choices.title: Test the full profile
choices.detail: Use all listed comparison costs, then tune from playtest telemetry.

choices.title: Lower only the Brush
choices.detail: Use 45 Essence for Brush but retain later costs until their routes are playable.

choices.title: Keep Brush at 150
choices.detail: Preserve the inherited first-hand cost despite its continuation pressure.

choices.title: Keep it unresolved
choices.detail: Do not choose the native Penmanship tuning profile yet.

questions.title: What should leaving a fight be called?
questions.context: Unbind is already the Binder's signature damage technique. Using the same word for leaving combat would put two unrelated actions in one palette. The current reversible build calls the tactical exit Withdraw and keeps Unbind as damage.
questions.recommendation: Keep Unbind for the distinctive Binder attack and use Withdraw for leaving the current fight. It describes a deliberate tactical choice without implying panic or ending the expedition.

choices.title: Use Withdraw
choices.detail: Unbind remains the damage technique; Withdraw leaves this encounter for the displayed Stability cost.

choices.title: Use Retreat
choices.detail: Keep Unbind as damage, but label the encounter exit Retreat.

choices.title: Use Flee
choices.detail: Keep Unbind as damage, but use the more urgent/failure-toned Flee label.

choices.title: Rename the attack
choices.detail: Reserve Unbind for leaving combat and choose a new name for the Binder's damage technique below.

questions.title: What level should a named traveller join at?
questions.context: Named travellers currently join at level 1 even late in a long campaign. Active members then earn the same XP, so the gap never closes naturally. Encounter scaling correctly does not lower foe level to protect a recruit, which can leave a late arrival permanently fragile or unusable.
questions.recommendation: Have each named traveller join at the Binder's current level. Recruitment is already a major earned reward, and immediate parity lets the new person be played instead of parked. Their authored calling lean remains a bonus, while all level-earned combat points arrive unspent so the player chooses the build.

choices.title: Match Binder level
choices.detail: Join immediately usable at the Binder's current level, with level points banked and authored lean preserved.

choices.title: Two levels behind
choices.detail: Join slightly behind and add accelerated XP until the traveller reaches the Binder; more growth texture, but another persistent rule.

choices.title: Level 1 with catch-up
choices.detail: Preserve a full growth arc but grant strongly accelerated XP; late recruits may still need to sit out initially.

choices.title: Keep level 1
choices.detail: Accept that late named travellers begin far behind and require ordinary equal-share XP to advance.

questions.title: Who chooses what survives a failed expedition?
questions.context: The current failure rule floors each inventory stack separately, so splitting the same haul across item types can make far more of it disappear. That arithmetic will be corrected regardless of this choice. The remaining design question is whether the game automatically chooses which exact items fit the corrected retention budget or lets you change a deterministic suggested set before confirming.
questions.recommendation: Let the player choose within the fixed budget. Show a deterministic suggested set first, then allow swaps without changing how many items survive. Bulk world resources remain automatically apportioned, while pages, knowledge, recruited people and pre-departure property keep their existing protection.

choices.title: Let me choose
choices.detail: Show a suggested retained set, then let the player swap exact acquired items within the same fixed budget before confirming.

choices.title: Choose automatically
choices.detail: Use the corrected total-unit budget but select retained items deterministically from the expedition outcome, with no extra decision screen.

choices.title: Protect favourites first
choices.detail: Choose automatically but prioritize items the player marked as favourites; simpler at failure time, but attachment must be predicted before the expedition.

choices.title: Test arithmetic first
choices.detail: Ship only the corrected automatic arithmetic, then revisit player choice after failure recaps are trustworthy.

questions.title: How should named characters grow distinct stats?
questions.context: Every named traveller currently starts with the same all-equal stats. Level-up raises the two currently highest stats, but an equal starting line has no authored tie identity, so distinct callings can converge on the same Might/Finesse build. This is separate from combat-tree lean and from the level a traveller joins at.
questions.recommendation: Give each named person an authored primary and secondary growth stat, let the Binder choose a pair at new game, and freeze a generated pair for generated companions. Add one point to each per level. This keeps growth legible and identity-specific without asking the player to assign points across a large roster.

choices.title: Authored stat pair
choices.detail: Each named person grows two authored stats; Binder chooses and generated companions freeze a generated pair.

choices.title: Weighted rotation
choices.detail: Give each character a five-stat order or weighting and rotate two increases per level; more varied, but harder to read.

choices.title: Assign every point
choices.detail: Let the player choose both stat increases at every level; strongest control, with substantial roster upkeep.

choices.title: Keep highest two
choices.detail: Retain current growth and add only a deterministic tie-breaking rule.

questions.title: What should Motes unlock in the Constellation?
questions.context: The old one-star Constellation only adds one Gambit slot. Your district idea gives the rare Mote currency a broader purpose without taxing every shop: three stars permit depths 4–5 of Offense, Defense, or Fieldcraft across the campaign, and three matching stars permit Tier-2 mastery in Commerce, Makers, or Commons. Every skill point, prerequisite, building, and ordinary upgrade cost still applies.
questions.recommendation: Use the matched 3+3 mastery structure plus the existing Long Instruction. Charge one Mote per broad permission in initial testing. This makes the three village directions and three combat trees rhyme without charging a Mote per person, node, or shop.

choices.title: Use both mastery trios
choices.detail: Offense/Defense/Fieldcraft and Commerce/Makers/Commons each get one broad one-Mote permission; keep Long Instruction separate.

choices.title: Combat mastery only
choices.detail: Motes permit depths 4–5 in the three combat trees; building mastery uses only ordinary construction progression.

choices.title: Keep one star only
choices.detail: Retain only the existing Gambit-capacity star and find a different role for Motes later.

questions.title: Should Constellation mastery cross separate save files?
questions.context: A Constellation permission can persist through any future Great-Work/Base cycle inside one campaign without automatically belonging to every new game. Making it account-wide would change fresh-save balance and make comparative testing less honest, while making it temporary would weaken the permanence fantasy.
questions.recommendation: Persist Constellation purchases in the individual campaign/save's Reality layer. A genuinely separate New Game begins clean; deleting that save deletes its mastery.

choices.title: One campaign/save
choices.detail: Mastery survives future cycles inside that campaign but never appears in another save slot.

choices.title: Across every save
choices.detail: Once bought, mastery applies to all current and future saves; stronger meta-progression, but fresh starts are no longer fresh.

choices.title: Decide with endgame
choices.detail: Keep the current Long Instruction behavior and hold broader persistence until Great Work cycles are actually designed.

questions.title: How much item and Field Kit capacity should remain after removing Workshop ladders?
questions.context: World Resources and Creature Materials no longer consume item slots, so nine shelving purchases and five +3 satchel rungs are repetitive. Existing saves can be preserved with a decode-only allowance even if the new campaign curve is smaller. This choice affects exact Items, World Pages, and prepared Field Kit families—not bulk resources.
questions.recommendation: Use Storehouse 16→28→40 and Field Kit 8→11→14→20, with Sela adding a separate +2. Old saves above 40/20 keep the difference as a non-purchasable legacy allowance. This is roomy without restoring a long mandatory capacity tax.

choices.title: Use 40 / 20 maxima
choices.detail: Two Storehouse upgrades and three pack projects; preserve larger old saves through a hidden legacy allowance.

choices.title: Keep old maxima
choices.detail: Compress to two/three large upgrades but end at 70 Storehouse and 23 Field Kit before Sela.

choices.title: Keep every rung
choices.detail: Retain nine shelving and five satchel purchases even though bulk resources no longer use those slots.

questions.title: How often should creature territories contain found objects?
questions.context: After an ordinary generated-creature victory, the game can make one rare territory-find roll for an object recovered from a den, nest, wrack or nearby trace. This is separate from guaranteed body-derived Creature materials, happens once per encounter rather than once per animal, and can never produce story objects, authored uniques or apex weapons.
questions.recommendation: Start with a 5% total chance: 3% ordinary campaign-banded gear, 1.5% eligible consumable and 0.5% ordinary Cache Key. At most one object appears, Teeming never adds rolls, and no essential progression depends on it.

choices.title: Rare mixed finds · 5%
choices.detail: Use 3% gear, 1.5% consumable, 0.5% Cache Key and 95% no find.

choices.title: More visible finds · 8%
choices.detail: Use 4% gear, 3% consumable, 1% Cache Key and 92% no find.

choices.title: Gear only · 3%
choices.detail: Keep the rare ordinary-gear find but exclude consumables and Cache Keys from creature territories.

choices.title: Hold territory finds
choices.detail: Use only body-derived Creature materials until the wider loot economy has more playtest evidence.
